resources.string: A passkey cannot be created in the app: a passkey belongs to the address of the web interface it is made under, and Android gives it to an app only with a permission on that domain (Digital Asset Links). Create new passkeys in the web interface in a browser; you can remove them here too.
This app gets its notifications through its pairing, not through Web Push. Listed here are the browsers in which you switched notifications on; switching on happens in each browser.

Device passwords for calendar and contacts
The iPhone logs in with your account name and a password of its own. Your account password and second factor never go onto the iPhone.
“%1$s” can no longer log in and syncs nothing any more. Calendars and contacts on the NAS stay. On the device, remove the account in the iOS settings.
One for each device: you lock out a lost iPhone on its own, the others keep working. To create one, TitanOS asks for your account password.
An account has at most %1$d devices. Revoke an old one to create a new one.
Visible only now. Enter it on the device right away; TitanOS keeps only a hash and cannot show it again.
